ShortDescription.Value: Does your city crash or show the "missing mods" warning since you removed mods or assets? This mod cleans the broken leftovers of missing content, so your save loads clean and runs stable.

Publish.LongDescription:
# Does your city crash ever since you made some changes to your playset?
It probably looks like this: you unsubscribe from a few mods or asset packs, your city still **seems to** work fine, nothing happens for an hour, maybe more... and then the game crashes to desktop (not very good). No error, no nothing, and YOU feel like you just wasted HUNDREDS of hours on a city just for it to get corrupted :( .
The reason? every object that removed content ever placed in your city — cars, props, surfaces, road markings — is still sitting in the save, pointing at something that no longer exists (because you uninstalled the mod). Sooner or later the simulation **touches** one of those broken leftovers and the game goes down (very bad).
It's exactly what happened to my city, and it's why I made this mod. If your save loads but keeps crashing after you changed your playset, there is a good chance it can be repaired with this mod (yippe!! your save is not gone forever :)).
# How to fix your save
1. Load the affected city. The mod scans it automatically and shows what it found in the mod's options (nothing is deleted yet, just showing what it found for now). 2. Press **"Repair now"** button (also in the mod's options) and confirm. 3. Save the city **under a new name** and keep the original file as a backup.
That's it. My city that kept crashing within an hour ran for hours afterwards without a single problem (yippe its fixed now).
# Keep it clean automatically
In the options there is also a **"Repair automatically on load"** toggle. (It's off by default so the first repair is always your own decision :) ) **I recommend** turning it on, because with automatic mode, you can **safely remove mods and assets without worrying about your save getting corrupted!** (hopefully, it worked for me but i didnt try every single mod, so it's possible something can still happen) (Keep in mind that if you load a save that was made with another playset, the automatic repair can delete some objects you might want to keep, so if you want to be safe, disable automatic repair and resubscribe to the mods for missing assets you want to keep, and then reenable or just press the repair button)
# Notes
- **Removal of objects is permanent in the repaired save.** If you re-subscribe to the removed mod later, the deleted objects will NOT come back (the repaired save no longer contains them). If you plan on adding a mod back, keep the original save! - This mod will **not** fix saves that are already corrupted and crash on load. It only works for saves that load normally and crash later. - The repair also tidies the save's internal list of mods that were ever used in it (the game only ever adds to that list). Don't be scared by the number, an old city easily has 100+ stale entries because most of them are just old versions of mods you still use. This is housekeeping, it doesn't change anything visible. - Your savegame file on disk is **never** touched. The repair happens in the loaded city and only becomes permanent when you save. - A detailed list of everything found (which missing asset, how many objects) is in `ModsData/CrashRepair/` and `Logs/CrashRepair.log`.
# Load menu still asks you to subscribe to a removed asset pack?
Deleting the placed objects is usually enough. The normal repair also takes care of the leftovers that would keep spawning broken objects: a vehicle model you picked for a transit line (the line uses random vehicles of its type again, as when none is chosen), trees you painted on a road (the road gets its default street trees back), and the map's list of required content. The scan result in the options tells you what it found.
Sometimes something else still points at the missing content: a company brand, a pending building upgrade, a policy, a service budget, a chirp. For those there is the **"Advanced cleanup"** toggle (off by default). Turn it on and press **"Repair now"** again, it fixes each of them the way the game itself would. When it is on, the automatic repair includes it too. It touches more than placed objects, so leave it off unless you need it. If the scan says a missing asset is held by data this mod doesn't handle (for example another mod's own data), the warning can't be removed by this mod.
Two more things the scan tells you. If a "missing" pack is only **disabled in your playset** (still subscribed), it leaves exactly the same traces as a removed one — the scan result says so; enable the pack instead of repairing if you want to keep its content. And if a missing asset belongs to a pack you still have **enabled**, the pack author removed or renamed it — the objects are just as broken and get repaired the same way, but there is nothing to subscribe to and the pack stays in the save's requirements (it is installed, so the load menu doesn't complain).
# How it works
The game keeps an empty placeholder for every missing asset a save references (most likely so that when you load a save with the wrong playset, it doesn't get fucked). Crash Repair finds all objects pointing at placeholders like that and deletes them through the game's regular bulldoze pipeline (so everything can clean up it's references properly). Only objects whose source content is **verifiably** missing are touched (runtime data the game manages itself (road compositions, effects, paths) is **explicitly** excluded from the scan).
Publish.ChangeLog: v1.2.0 - The repair now also clears the leftovers that keep spawning broken objects and keep the load menu asking for a removed pack: vehicle models chosen for transit lines, trees painted on roads, and the map's list of required content. - New "Advanced cleanup" option (off by default; applies to "Repair now" and, when on, to the automatic repair) for the remaining data that can point at missing content: company brands, pending building upgrades, policies, service budgets and chirps. Each is handled the way the game itself would. - The scan now reports all of those, tells you when a missing asset is held by data the mod doesn't handle, when a "missing" pack is merely disabled in your playset, and when a missing asset was dropped from a pack you still have enabled. - The scan result in the options is shown one finding per line, and the log lists every repaired road, junction, building and vehicle. - Junctions switched to another road type get that type's node tags, and buildings that fronted a deleted road are registered with it so the game finds them a new road. - Deleting a transit line with a missing prefab now also deletes its waypoints and segments, like the game's own bulldoze does. - Roads of a missing road type are now removed the way the bulldozer does it: junctions that other roads still use are kept and switched to a remaining road type instead of being destroyed (that crashed the game). - The repair now runs through the same frame path as bulldozing, so the game's own cleanup of lots, driveways and owned vehicles applies. The automatic repair scans at load and runs a moment later, once the city is fully set up. - Wording fix: the mod-list tidy-up from v1.1.0 is housekeeping, it doesn't affect the load menu warning.
